text:
alex: hey team, day 1 q — what's the recommended pattern for using Redwood keys in local dev + CI? don't want to accidentally commit a hosted key or have flaky 429s during CI matrix runs.
priya: welcome! :wave: short rules: never commit hosted prod keys. For casual dev use the sandbox key. For CI use per-repo service tokens stored in SecretsManager (rotate them). If you need high concurrency for demos, request a short-lived hosted dev key.
devex-bot: docs: https://internal.redwood.devex/keys-and-quotas  see "CI patterns" and "Temporary dev keys". To request keys: https://internal.redwood.devex/requests/keys (include team, window, expected RPS/streams).
ben: practical tips: 1) gate heavy e2e by checking X-RateLimit-Remaining or GET /v1/account/limits before starting. 2) clamp parallel workers in CI and add retry/backoff for 429s. 3) for streaming demos either request concurrency explicitly or use recorded streams.
alex: any short code snippet for gating in CI?
priya: example bash step: 
REMAIN=$(curl -s -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | grep -Fi X-RateLimit-Remaining | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d '\\r')
if [ -z "$REMAIN" ] || [ "$REMAIN" -lt 100 ]; then echo "skip heavy e2e: low quota ($REMAIN)"; exit 0; fi
infra-bot: note: sandbox has lower token/sec and concurrent stream caps; ephemeral tokens are available for per-job tokens: https://internal.redwood.devex/ephemeral-tokens.
alex: thanks — i'll set up SecretsManager for CI and open a temporary hosted key request for our demo if needed. appreciate it :thumbsup:
